title: Coral and the Prom
premise: Ivo Underhill, the only out kid in the fishing town of Coral, has survived fifteen years by being careful—until cleaning out their grandmother's recipe box reveals cards written in her hand that aren't recipes at all, but instructions for a magic that runs beneath the town like an old tide. The cards name Ivo as the next keeper of Coral's luck, a power their grandmother fed quietly for decades at a cost she hid in the margins. As prom approaches and the town's luck begins to sour without a keeper, Ivo must learn the craft from the cards while dodging the town council's charming, corrupt chairwoman, who wants the power for herself and knows exactly how to weaponize a small town against one queer kid. In the end, Ivo refuses both invisibility and inherited control, unbinding the luck so it belongs to no one—and walks into prom as themselves, paying the price of survival by finally refusing to pay it.
about_author: Jude Zhou grew up in a coastal town where everyone claimed to know everyone's business and nobody actually knew anything. They write stories about small places, sharp secrets, and kids who outgrow the labels handed to them.

chapters.title: The Recipe Box
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Clearing out Grandma Ruthie's kitchen after the funeral, Ivo finds recipe cards that read less like cooking and more like ritual—one card is addressed to 'the next of us.' The emotional beat: grief sharpening into unease, the first crack in the careful life Ivo has built.

chapters.title: Nine Hundred Witnesses
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. A week back at school shows how Coral watches its only out kid: kind enough to be suffocating, cruel enough to remember. Best friend Dana insists prom will be fine; Ivo knows better. Beat: establishing the cost of visibility and why Ivo learned to disappear.

chapters.title: Cards That Aren't for Food
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Testing a card half-jokingly on the garden, Ivo coaxes tomatoes out of frozen ground overnight. Terror and wonder arrive together. Beat: the moment 'staying invisible was never really an option' becomes literal.

chapters.title: What Grandma Fed
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV, with letters interspersed. Hidden correspondence reveals Ruthie was Coral's 'keeper,' feeding the town's luck through quiet workings—and hiding what it took from her. Beat: inheritance reframed as burden; Ivo realizes the care they inherited has teeth.

chapters.title: The Chairwoman's Smile
chapters.summary: Council chairwoman Marla Voss invites Ivo to tea, all warmth and implication: she knew Ruthie's 'civic contributions' and expects continuity. She mentions Ivo's 'situation' with a smile that isn't one. Beat: power introduces itself as kindness.

chapters.title: Practice in the Dark
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Nightly experiments behind the cannery ruins; Dana catches them mid-working and, instead of flinching, asks to help. Beat: first alliance, first relief—the luxury of being seen by one person.

chapters.title: Luck Runs Thin
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Without a keeper, Coral sours: boats come back empty, the cannery lays off workers, a boy breaks his arm on dry pavement. Whispers start about Ruthie's death 'breaking something.' Beat: the town's hunger makes refusal feel like betrayal.

chapters.title: Margins and Marginalia
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Deciphering Ruthie's marginal notes, Ivo learns each working drew from the keeper's own years, memories, self. Ruthie didn't die of age; she spent herself. Beat: horror and love tangled—Ivo understands the price of survival was paid in secret.

chapters.title: Prom Committee Politics
chapters.summary: Dana's POV. Prom planning becomes a battlefield when Voss's son proposes a 'traditional couples only' ticket policy aimed squarely at Ivo bringing a date. Beat: the ordinary cruelty of small-town democracy, and Dana learning to fight loud.

chapters.title: The Offer
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Voss offers protection—real protection, tickets fixed, bullies handled—in exchange for training her as the next keeper. She frames it as rescue. Beat: temptation with a familiar face; Ivo recognizes the trade they've made their whole life: safety for self.

chapters.title: A Date, Declared
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ivo asks Theo, the new kid who fixes boats and doesn't flinch, to prom—in front of people. It goes wrong in ways both petty and painful, but Ivo doesn't retract it. Beat: choosing visibility while terrified; the theme made flesh.

chapters.title: Backlash
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Vandalism, a sermon, Dad's exhausted disappointment: 'Why do you have to make everything hard?' Ivo nearly takes Voss's deal. Beat: the lowest point of the middle—the price of survival itemized.

chapters.title: Ruthie's Last Card
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Behind the false bottom of the box, a final card: 'If you're reading this, refuse.' Ruthie's instructions for unbinding the luck entirely—dangerous, unfinished, forbidden by every keeper before. Beat: hope with a warning label.

chapters.title: Voss Moves First
chapters.summary: Marla's POV. Impatient, Voss steals three cards from Ivo's room and attempts a working alone; it feeds on her ambition and starts curdling the town's luck into something meaner. Beat: power and its corruption dramatized; the antagonist becomes a cautionary mirror.

chapters.title: The Tide Turns Ugly
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Coral turns on itself—fights at the diner, the harbor fouling overnight, a mob mentality forming around 'who broke the luck.' Suspicion lands on Ivo. Beat: rising tension peaks; the town's fear needs a target and picks the usual one.

chapters.title: Cornered at the Cannery
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Confronted by the council and half the town at the cannery ruins, Ivo is given an ultimatum: bind the luck under council control or leave. Dana and Theo stand with them publicly. Beat: the labels come off—there is no invisible left to retreat to.

chapters.title: Reading the Whole Box
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. All-night study with Dana and Theo; they reconstruct Ruthie's unbinding rite and discover it requires a keeper to give up the power willingly and name what it cost them. Beat: preparation, intimacy, resolve—the calm before climax.

chapters.title: Prom
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ivo goes to prom anyway, in the outfit they want, with Theo, while Voss works her stolen cards in the gym's back hall. Halfway through the night the lights gutter, the music warps. Beat: joy and danger braided; the party as battleground.

chapters.title: The Working War
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Climax. Ivo confronts Voss mid-rite; her borrowed power turns on her hunger. Ivo begins the unbinding as the gym watches, speaking aloud what the keeping cost Ruthie and would cost them. Beat: sacrifice offered, corruption exposed before witnesses.

chapters.title: Unbound
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. The luck releases—not destroyed, but freed into the town itself, belonging to everyone and no one. Voss collapses into ordinariness; the tide steadies. Beat: catharsis; the price of survival refused and survived.

chapters.title: Aftertide
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Coral adjusts to ordinariness—harder seasons, honest ones. Dad tries, badly then better. Voss resigns. Ivo keeps exactly one card: not a spell, just Ruthie's handwriting saying 'proud of you.' Beat: quiet reckoning with inheritance redefined.

chapters.title: Slow Dance
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. A make-up dance in Dana's backyard—string lights, the whole found circle, Theo's hand in theirs. Ivo decides to stay in Coral, visible, on purpose. Beat: resolution; the kid who survived by hiding chooses to remain by standing still.
